title: Expire pending orders and release reservations idempotently
verify: The Medusa cron job finds only native pending orders with logical pending_payment metadata and an expired UTC timestamp.
Expiration cancels the order through the supported Medusa workflow and releases reservations by order line without direct stock mutation.
Paid, canceled, non-pending, and not-yet-expired orders are unchanged.
Repeated job/workflow execution is idempotent and completes cleanup after a simulated partial failure.
The 72-hour window is calculated in UTC with deterministic clock/test coverage and sanitized operational evidence.
T3 verification records semantic-pass, HUMAN_CHECKPOINT: done, and ROLLBACK_RECOVERY_NOTE: present.

verify.scheduler_recommendation: Leave in_progress pending required T3 per-task semantic-pass and closure markers.

verify.reason: Adversarial review confirmed native cancellation owns normal reservation deletion, cleanup retries remain consistent, guarded states are preserved, and no forbidden cross-feature or production behavior was introduced.

evidence_required: Integration evidence for expired, paid, canceled, and partial-cleanup fixtures.
Reservation count/stock evidence before and after cancellation with no duplicate release.
Cron/workflow retry evidence and sanitized logs without customer data or secrets.
Typecheck/build/lint output and full T3 protocol, semantic, checkpoint, and rollback evidence.
constraints: Never cancel a paid or non-pending order from the expiry job.
Cancel first and release reservations through native APIs so partial cleanup remains retryable.
Do not add a custom queue, scheduler service, inventory ledger, or payment-provider behavior.
Do not use wall-clock behavior without deterministic expiry calculation tests.
invariants: Unpaid pending orders expire after exactly 72 hours according to server UTC time.
Each reservation is released at most once.
Terminal order state and reservation cleanup are safe to retry.
Ambiguous payment/order state stops automatic mutation.
purpose: Provide the durable 72-hour timeout and reservation-release boundary required by pending-payment orders.
success_outcome: Expired pending orders are canceled and their holds released exactly once, with safe retries and no effect on paid orders.
anti_goals: Do not implement YooKassa webhook or payment retry behavior.
Do not finalize reservations on payment success; that downstream handoff belongs to FT-009.
Do not hide partial cleanup failures or claim success from a job log alone.

forbidden_scope: FT-009 payment-provider calls, webhook, or credentials
production data, secrets, direct browser database access
stop_conditions: The job cannot distinguish logical pending_payment from paid/non-pending orders.
Reservation cleanup is not retryable after a partial failure.
The installed Medusa cancellation/reservation APIs contradict the linked specs.
Verification cannot prove unchanged paid-order state.
